summary: A US-Iran deal to extend the ceasefire and gradually restore Persian Gulf energy exports pulled oil prices lower and eased bond yields, even as PCE inflation rose to a three-year high and consumer spending stayed robust. Long-dated Treasuries have faced sustained pressure since the war's outbreak, with the 30-year yield spiking above 5% this month before attracting buyers, keeping real rates elevated and gold on the back foot.
tweet: A US-Iran ceasefire extension is easing oil and bond yields, but PCE at a 3-year high keeps rate-cut hopes in check — stocks greed, gold fear, bonds neutral.
